correctness.rationale: The centroid-in-sampled-hull event is affine invariant under mapping of each chosen edge parameter to the reference triangle. The two exhaustive nonzero occupancy types give exact integrals \\(1/9+4\\log2/27\\) and \\(2\\log 2/3\\); the multinomial occupancy sum reduces to the proposed symmetric polynomial. Strict side inequalities \\(0<p_i<1/2\\) prove the unattained lower bound; AM-GM plus Cauchy inequalities prove upper equality precisely at the equilateral triangle. Pairwise averaging strictly increases the second elementary symmetric polynomial and does not decrease the third. SymPy integrations and independent Euclidean Monte Carlo confirm crucial expressions; finite simulation is not taken as proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The centroid containment event is invariant under positive radial rescaling, so interior-uniform sampling is equivalent to sampling each edge with weight 1/3 and uniform fractional coordinate. Euclidean perimeter-uniform sampling instead has edge weights equal to normalized side lengths, generally not 1/3. This changes the law and is not an equivalent formulation unless the triangle is equilateral.

originality.rationale: Directly inspected Prékopa (1972) on the equilateral case and interior-uniform triangle model; this proves the upper-end constant but not a shape-dependent arclength boundary law over all triangles. Ionascu (2016/2019) treats interior-uniform planar regions and nonuniform radial projection densities. The one-point-per-side term \\(2\\log 2/3\\) is credited to a 2021 full derivation. Wendel (1962) assumes centrally symmetric random vectors, which triangular perimeter sampling violates. A related discrete-regular-polygon study concerns a different law. The arbitrary edge-weight symmetric polynomial and strict Schur-concavity with sharp nonattained infimum were absent from inspected readable full texts and targeted research-record searches. Priority remains provisional; full Halasz--Kleitman 1974 was not accessible.

value.rationale: The result solves the natural fully specified probability for a genuine arclength-uniform random triangle on every triangular boundary. Although the equilateral constant is classical, the physical-versus-affine side-weight distinction produces a nonconstant geometric invariant with a complete sharp shape range and strict majorization principle, plus an arbitrary-edge-weight formula clarifying the classical shape-independent sampling law. The class and boundary limits are geometrically natural rather than arbitrary numerical cuts.
